title: Best Friedrich Dehumidifier (2026): D35B1B vs. D50B1B + Recall
h1: The Best Friedrich Dehumidifiers — and the Recall to Check First
dek: Friedrich’s two current models both come with a built-in pump. Older units under the same names deserve a closer look before you buy.
description: The best Friedrich dehumidifier for 2026: the D35B1B and D50B1B compared, plus how to check older D50BP and D70BP units against the 2021 fire recall.
intro: A **Friedrich dehumidifier** comes from a San Antonio company best known for window and PTAC air conditioners, and its dehumidifiers carry some of that HVAC thinking. The current lineup is just two models — the **35-pint D35B1B** and the **50-pint D50B1B** — and both include a built-in condensate pump plus a five-year warranty on the sealed refrigeration system.

There’s one complication worth knowing before you shop. A 2021 recall covered several older Friedrich models, including the D50BP and D70BP, for fire and burn hazards. Those model names still show up in retail listings, so the name alone won’t tell you whether a particular unit is affected.
Below we cover the two current models, explain exactly how to check an older unit, and include a pump-equipped alternative if Friedrich’s range doesn’t fit your space.
topPicksLead: For most mid-size damp rooms, the **Friedrich 35-Pint D35B1B** is the one to buy, with a built-in pump and ENERGY STAR efficiency.

products.whyWeLoveIt: A built-in pump is unusual at 35 pints, and it’s the reason to choose this Friedrich. Run a hose up to a sink or out a window and you never touch the bucket again — handy in a basement corner with no floor drain.
products.performance: It’s rated at 35 pints a day, with retailers typically listing coverage around 800–1,000 sq ft. The pump can push water vertically, horizontally or a combination of both up to 15 feet, and there’s a 16.2-pint bucket if you’d rather not use it. This generation switched to R-32 refrigerant, replacing the earlier D35B1A.

blocks.text: We don’t lab-test dehumidifiers. For this guide we checked Friedrich’s current product pages and manuals, ENERGY STAR listings, the CPSC recall notice and published independent bench reviews, then read owner reviews for reliability patterns.
Because Friedrich’s range is small, we also looked hard at what you can’t get from it — a 70-pint model, for instance — and added an alternative so every reader leaves with a workable option.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Friedrich dehumidifier

items.label: The current model number
items.text: The D35B1B and D50B1B are Friedrich’s current units. An “A” suffix or BP-series name signals older stock.

items.label: A manufacture date outside 2009–2017
items.text: For any D50BP, D70BP or similar listing, check the date or serial number on the unit against the recall notice before buying.

items.label: Honest sizing
items.text: Friedrich tops out at 50 pints. For a very wet basement, our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) will tell you if you need more.

items.label: A drain route for the pump
items.text: Plan where the hose will go — a sink, window or standpipe within 15 feet of combined lift.

items.label: The warranty in writing
items.text: Register the unit so the five-year sealed-system coverage is easy to claim.

blocks.text: In 2021 the CPSC announced a recall of roughly 2 million dehumidifiers made by New Widetech and sold under 20 brand names, including Friedrich, Danby, Honeywell, Haier and Whirlpool, after more than 100 reports of units overheating or catching fire.

The Friedrich models listed were the **D25ANP, D25BNP, D25D, D25DA, D50AP, D50BP, D50BP-A, D50D, D70AP, D70BP, D70BP-A and D70D**, made between January 1, 2009 and August 31, 2017. The remedy is a refund through the recall program’s website or hotline listed on the CPSC notice.

blocks.title: Why the model name isn’t enough
blocks.text: Some retailers still list D50BP and D70BP units, new or refurbished. The recall covers a manufacture window, not the name forever, so only the date code or serial number on the unit settles it. Friedrich’s own current lineup no longer includes these models.

items: Find the rating label on the back or side of the unit.
Note the model number and manufacture date or serial number.
Compare them against the CPSC recall notice for New Widetech dehumidifiers.
If it’s covered, unplug it and stop using it, then file for the refund.

blocks.text: Published bench reviews of the previous-generation D50BP praised two things: an unusually accurate built-in humidity reading — within about 1% of actual room humidity — and quiet running. Moisture removal and efficiency landed mid-pack.

Durability was the weak spot. About a quarter of owner reviews for that older model cited reliability problems, even as many praised Friedrich’s customer service. The current D35B1B and D50B1B are a newer generation, but the five-year sealed-system warranty is worth registering for all the same.

sections.heading: Is a Friedrich dehumidifier worth it?

blocks.text: It depends on how much you value the pump. Most 35-pint dehumidifiers drain to a bucket or a gravity hose only, so they’re stuck near a floor drain or need emptying once or twice a day in a damp room. Friedrich puts a pump in both of its models, which lets you place the unit where the moisture is rather than where the drain is.

Against that, you’re paying a premium over mainstream 35- and 50-pint units, the range is small, and reliability feedback on the previous generation was mixed. If your basement has a floor drain right beside the dehumidifier spot, a gravity-draining unit from our [best dehumidifier with drain hose](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-drain-hose/) list saves money. If it doesn’t, a Friedrich — registered for its five-year sealed-system coverage — is a sensible buy.

blocks.title: Pump upkeep tip
blocks.text: Every few months, flush the pump reservoir with a little warm water and check the hose for kinks or algae. A blocked outlet is the most common reason pump dehumidifiers stop draining.

The **Friedrich D35B1B** is the right pick for a mid-size damp room, and the **D50B1B** handles a larger basement — both with a built-in pump and a five-year sealed-system warranty. If you’re considering an older D50BP or D70BP, check its manufacture date against the 2021 recall first. Need more capacity than 50 pints, or a model that’s easier to find? The **GE APER50LZ** is a solid pump-equipped alternative, and our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) guide covers the wider field.

faqs.q: What is the best Friedrich dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a mid-size damp room, the 35-pint D35B1B. For a larger basement or wetter space, the 50-pint D50B1B. Both have a built-in pump with up to 15 feet of lift, digital 30–90% humidity control and a five-year sealed-system warranty.

faqs.q: Has a Friedrich dehumidifier been recalled?
faqs.a: Yes. A 2021 recall covered Friedrich models including the D25ANP, D25BNP, D25D, D25DA, D50AP, D50BP, D50BP-A, D50D, D70AP, D70BP, D70BP-A and D70D made between January 2009 and August 2017, due to fire and burn hazards. Affected owners are eligible for a refund.

faqs.q: Is it safe to buy a Friedrich D50BP or D70BP today?
faqs.a: Only after checking the manufacture date or serial number against the recall notice. Units built after August 31, 2017 aren’t covered, but the model name alone can’t tell you when a unit was made.

faqs.q: Does Friedrich still make a 70-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: No. The current range stops at 50 pints a day. If you need more capacity, see our [best 70-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-70-pint-dehumidifier/) picks.

faqs.q: Where can I find a Friedrich dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Friedrich posts owner’s manuals and installation guides on the product page for each model on its website. Have the full model number from the unit’s rating label handy, since manuals differ between generations such as the D50B1A and D50B1B.

faqs.q: What is the Friedrich dehumidifier warranty?
faqs.a: One year of parts and labor, plus five years of limited coverage on the sealed refrigeration system — the compressor and related components — on both current models.
